## About

These are the cases of the three R setups, [selected images, lightbox
on](b-panzoom-lightbox.html), [global panzoom](c-panzoom-auto.html), and
[selected images only](d-panzoom-selective.html), opened by lightbox without
panzoom. Compare each case with the same number there. Every block image opens
in lightbox, with these settings:

```yaml
lightbox:
  match: auto
  effect: fade
  desc-position: right
  loop: true
  css-class: my-lb
```

## 1. Single image {#c1 expect-open="glightbox"}

```markdown {.show-source}
![A markdown image with a description and `desc-position="left"`. It opens in lightbox with the description on the left.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){description="Chilmark has _some_ of the best beaches. **credit:** [Chilmark Beach](https://unsplash.com/photos/VBDJGOMCwps)" desc-position="left" fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## 2. Gallery in a layout {#c2 expect-open="glightbox"}

```markdown {.show-source}
::: {layout="[[1, 1], [1]]"}
![Aquinnah, one of three images joined by `group`. They open in lightbox as a three-image gallery.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){group="elsewhere" description="The waves break off Aquinnah." fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}

![Oak Bluffs, in the same gallery.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){group="elsewhere" description="Gingerbread cottages." fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}

![Vineyard lighthouse, in the same gallery.](../../images/mv-2.jpg){group="elsewhere" description="Edgartown Lighthouse." fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}
:::
```

## 3. Math {#c3 expect-open="glightbox"}

A markdown image with math in its caption and description. It opens in lightbox
with both typeset.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Caption with math $e^{i\pi}+1=0$](../../images/mv-4.jpg){description="Description with math $\\int_0^1 x^2\\,dx = 1/3$" fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach"}
```

## 4. Markdown subfigures {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

```markdown {.show-source}
::: {#fig-md-sub layout-ncol=2}
![Sub A](../../images/mv-1.jpg){#fig-md-a fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}

![Sub B](../../images/mv-2.jpg){#fig-md-b fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}

Two markdown subfigures, the first cross-referenced here (see @fig-md-a). They open in lightbox as a two-image gallery.
:::
```

## 5. R subfigures {#c5 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{r}
#| label: fig-r-sub
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Two subfigures from one R cell. They open in lightbox as a two-image
#|   gallery.
#| fig-subcap: ["Pressure", "Cars"]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#|   - "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| layout-ncol: 2

plot(pressure)
plot(cars)
```

## 6. Cell options {#c6 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of ten random points"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   An R cell with lightbox options for a group and a description. It opens in
#|   lightbox, in a two-image gallery with the next plot.
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: This is 1 to 10 plot

plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   The second R cell in the same group. It opens in lightbox, in the same
#|   gallery.
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: We see our cars data above

plot(cars)
```

## 7. Two plots in one cell {#c7 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{r}
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Scatterplot matrix of the mtcars data, each variable plotted against every other"
#|   - "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| fig-cap:
#|   - >-
#|     One R cell with two plots, and a caption and description for each. They
#|     open in lightbox as a two-image gallery.
#|   - "The second plot of the cell, in the same gallery."
#| lightbox:
#|   group: cars
#|   description:
#|     - Description for first graph
#|     - Description for second graph

plot(mtcars)
plot(cars)
```

## 8. Opt out {#c8 expect-open="nothing"}

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "An R cell with `lightbox: false`. Clicking it does nothing."
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Scatterplot matrix of the mtcars data, each variable plotted against every
#|   other

plot(mtcars)
```

## 9. Image in a link {#c9 expect-open="nothing"}

An image inside a link. Quarto turns it into a figure and drops the link, so
clicking it does nothing.

```markdown {.show-source}
[![Linked image](../../images/mv-4.jpg){width=30%}](https://quarto.org){aria-label="Quarto website"}
```

## 10. Margin image {#c10 expect-open="glightbox"}

```markdown {.show-source}
![A markdown image in the margin. It opens in lightbox.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.column-margin fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}
```

## 11. Inline image {#c11 expect-open="nothing"}

An image inside a sentence. lightbox skips inline images, so clicking it does
nothing.

```markdown {.show-source}
Some text with an inline image ![A white lighthouse](../../images/mv-2.jpg){width=60px} in the middle.
```

## 12. Plain R figure {#c12 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{r}
#| label: fig-plain
#| fig-alt: "Heat map of the Maunga Whau volcano's heights, in yellow, orange, and red"
#| fig-cap: "A cross-referenced R figure with no options. It opens in lightbox."

image(volcano)
```
